March 4, 2025
Hon. Donna Bailey, Chair Hon. Kristi Mathieson, Chair Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Cross Building, Room 220 Augusta, ME 04333
Re: Testimony in support of L.D. 645, An Act to Change the Size and Composition of the Board of Directors of the Maine Health Data Organization
Dear Senator Bailey and Representative Mathieson,
Please accept this testimony on behalf of the Office of the Governor in support of L.D. 645, An Act to Change the Size and Composition of the Board of Directors of the Maine Health Data Organization.
The Maine Health Data Organization (MHDO) is an independent executive agency established to create and maintain a comprehensive health information database and issue various reports used to improve the health of Maine people. The MHDO operates under the supervision of a Board of Directors, which sets the priorities and guiding principles for the organization and carries out various duties set in statute.
Over the course of years, MHDO has provided wide-ranging data for use in analyzing health costs, utilization, and outcomes. They have issued a number of reports that have been relied on by the Legislature as well as the Executive branch on issues ranging from prescription drug pricing, the Maine Cancer Blueprint, behavioral health, and more.
L.D. 645 proposes to alter the size of the Board decreasing it from twenty-one members to thirteen members, to change the composition of the board, and to remove the staggering of initial terms. The Governor's office supports these updates and has every confidence that a more streamlined Board will improve efficiency while maintaining the high level of quality work that MHDO has been able to produce. The Governor's office urges the Committee's support for this bill and thanks you for your consideration.
Sincerely,
Joe Boucher Director of Boards and Commissions

I have been a member of the board of directors for the Maine Health Data Organization (MHDO) for almost ten years, and for the last two years have sen/ed as the Chair of the
board. The MHDO was established in 1995 as an independent executive agency governed
by a multi-stakeholder board of directors as defined in Title 22, Chapter 1683; and its purpose is to create and maintain a useful, objective, reliable, and comprehensive health information database that is used to improve the health of Maine citizens and to issue reports promoting public transparency of health care quality, outcomes, and costs. The
MHDO makes data publicly available and accessible to the broadest extent consistent with

these meetings verbally or in writing in opposition to the proposed changes.
The substantive changes in LD 645 include reducing the size of the board from 20 voting
members to a board with 12 voting members. The reductions were made in the number of

10035656:
Testimony of Trevor Putnoky to the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services
In Support of
LD 645, An Act to Change the Size and Composition of the Board of Directors of the Maine Health Data Organization
March 4, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services.
My name is Trevor Putnoky and I'm the President and CEO of the Healthcare Purchaser Alliance of Maine. The HPA is a nonprofit that represents the purchasers of health care in Maine. Our mission is to advance and support access to high-quality, affordable care. We have over 60 members, including some of the largest public and private employers and health trusts in Maine. Collectively, our members spend over a billion dollars annually providing health care for nearly one quarter of the commercially insured population in the state.
I'm here today to testify in support of LD 645 and to urge the committee to support this thoughtful reconfiguration the Maine Health Data Organization (MHDO) board.
We're extremely fortunate to have such a high caliber and comprehensive all-payer claims database here in Maine. The data, analyses, and reports produced by MHDO are tremendous and essential resources for policy makers, healthcare providers, healthcare purchasers, consumers, and researchers in Maine. And as the healthcare landscape and the challenges facing our system evolve, MHDO has expanded and adapted the information that it makes available so that users can better leverage its data to understand healthcare cost drivers in Maine and improve affordability for families and employers in our state.
While MHDO's Board has done an effective job balancing the impacts of reporting requirements against the aim of making key information broadly available, I believe that the reconfiguration proposed in LD 645 would allow for a more efficient governance structure and process, while at the same time preserving robust representation of the different stakeholders who are affected by MHDO's data submission requirements or who utilize the information that MHDO produces and posts for public consumption.
Thank you for the opportunity to share our support for LD 645 and for the important work of the MHDO. I'd be happy to answer any questions and will be available for the work session.
